title: 50agents vs n8n: self-hosted or built for you | 50agents
description: n8n is a self-hostable workflow builder with code nodes and per-run pricing; 50agents builds automations, AI agents and apps from plain words.
answer: Pick n8n if you are technical, want to self-host, need code nodes, or run long workflows where paying once per run matters.
Pick 50agents if the people who need the work done will describe it rather than build it; it is free to start, with no server to run.
ask: Set up an automation: every new Stripe payment is added as a row to my Google Sheet with the customer, amount and date
lede: n8n wins every row a developer cares about: self-hosting, a Code node, JSON export and a node canvas you control.

us: Nobody on the team will maintain a server or a canvas.
You want an app, such as a leads tracker or an invoices desk, as well as automations, from the same place.
You want to start free, without picking a plan or a server first.
them: Data must stay on your own servers.
You need code, custom HTTP calls or nodes you write yourself.
Your workflows are long and run often; one execution per run is hard to beat.

move.title: Keep the JSON
move.body: Download each workflow as JSON before you change anything.

move.title: Move the business workflows, keep the technical ones
move.body: Workflows with Code nodes and custom HTTP stay in n8n. Workflows a non-developer keeps asking to change are the ones to rebuild in 50agents.

move.title: Describe, test, switch
move.body: Tell Captain the outcome, check the test run against n8n's last execution, then deactivate the n8n workflow.

faqs.a: No. 50agents is hosted only. If self-hosting is a requirement, n8n or Activepieces fit.
n8n's directory lists 2,829 integrations; 50agents works with 2,300+ through viaSocket.
No. Automations are made of fixed blocks, and Captain writes no code. If a workflow needs code, keep it in n8n.
